analysis.investment_thesis: Cigniti is a profitable, near-debt-free niche quality-engineering firm with strong ROCE of 34% and improving margins, but revenue growth has decelerated sharply to ~10-11% in FY24-25 — well below my 20-30% threshold for exceptional growers. The Coforge acquisition creates strategic optionality but clouds the independent growth narrative.
key_strengths: Near-pristine balance sheet: D/E of 0.02, cash of INR 199 Cr in FY25, and FCF positive all 5 years
Exceptional capital efficiency: ROCE 34.1% and ROE 26% signal a genuinely high-quality services business
Niche positioning in AI/digital assurance and QE is aligned with enterprise digital transformation spending
key_risks: Revenue growth deceleration: from 33% in FY23 to just 10-11% in FY24-25 — the wrong direction for a Fisher holding
AI-driven test automation threatens to commoditize manual and semi-automated testing services at scale
Coforge subsidiary status limits independent strategic management decisions — a key Fisher concern
red_flags: 9-year revenue CAGR of 14.5% falls below my 20% minimum; more critically, recent years show momentum loss
The catastrophic FY2017 loss (-INR 395 Cr net profit, likely goodwill impairment) reveals historical management quality lapses
Capex is negligible (INR 14 Cr on INR 2,014 Cr revenue) — minimal R&D reinvestment signals a harvesting rather than growth posture
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From my scuttlebutt lens, Cigniti occupies a real niche — pure-play software testing and quality engineering is a defensible specialization, and their foray into AI assurance, 5G testing, and digital engineering is the right strategic direction. The financials are genuinely respectable: operating margins expanded to 17.09%, EBITDA grew from INR 134 Cr in FY22 to INR 294 Cr in FY25, and the balance sheet transformation from INR 121 Cr borrowings in FY20 to a near-zero debt position is admirable. At P/E of 11.7x and EV/EBITDA of 9.06x, the market is pricing this as a slow-growth commodity IT services firm — not entirely unfair given recent numbers.

What stops me from being enthusiastic is exactly what I look for most: accelerating innovation-driven growth. Revenue grew only 10.4% in FY25, and while margins are expanding, the top-line is not compounding at rates that produce the wealth I seek. More importantly, being subsumed by Coforge in December 2024 raises deep questions about independent management vision — one of my non-negotiable criteria. The company has a fine business, but fine businesses at moderate growth rates with uncertain management independence are HOLD situations, not the great growth stories I build concentrated positions in.
